problem.text: LinearEXL3.get_tensors used repeated assignments and different inclusion rules for ordinary tensors and decoder-multiplier metadata.

reasoning.text: The cleanup centralizes export in one comprehension: enumerate known attributes, exclude None, prefix each name with the layer key, and make every exported tensor contiguous. This reduces repetition but is not strictly behavior-preserving.

impact.text: Present mcg and mul1 tensors are now exported even when their decoded multiplier is zero; previously their integer truth value controlled inclusion. Both metadata tensors also gain contiguous() normalization. Constructor decoding and inference calls remain unchanged.

source_notes.text: Read the initial quantized-inference entry and the experimental-codebook entry d359bcc. They establish the earlier loading/export interface and the introduction of per-tensor multiplier metadata, respectively.

Issue #11, “AssertionError: bias is wrong datatype,” reports a constructor failure and subsequent successful fix. Its contextual relationship is inferred from the same exl3.py constructor; the inspected parent already converts FP32 bias to half, and this task changes only export.

PR #26, “Superior 3INST parameters,” discusses alternative codebooks and explicitly identifies d359bcc as their implementation. Its relationship to this cleanup is inferred specifically from mcg/mul1 metadata, not an explicit reference to the task commit.

Other discussions matching inspected conversion paths concern distinct failures: #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” concerns native-extension loading; #33, “Error converting model,” develops from file-opening failures into a GLM sampling report; #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” and #42, “converting to 3.0 bpw causes error; block state has 0 inf values and 34 NaN values,” concern factorization/nonfinite-state failures. Their contextual links are inferred from shared source paths, not evidence that this export cleanup fixes them.

limitations: No PyTorch tensor operation, serialization round trip, model conversion or GPU execution was tested. The bounded check used fake tensor objects and a transcription of the new comprehension.
Repository searches establish visible callers, not dynamic or external consumers. No performance improvement is measured.

claims.text: get_tensors retains the key argument and dictionary return interface. Its candidate list contains su, sv, suh, svh, trellis, bias, mcg and mul1; each non-None value becomes tensor.contiguous() under key.subkey. The obsolete commented scale export disappears.

The uniform None filter also replaces unconditional trellis export. For normally constructed instances this does not weaken the required-trellis invariant: __init__ still asserts trellis is present. It stores unpacked suh/svh and sets su/sv to None, so ordinary exports contain the unpacked representation.

The removed multiplier truth checks previously omitted zero-valued metadata. The replacement preserves presence instead of testing decoder selection. Linear.load_exl3 reads either optional tensor and __init__ decodes its unsigned value, with absence defaulting to zero. create_quantization_config_json still lists stored tensors but emits named multiplier fields only for nonzero values; it therefore accepts the newly retained zero tensors without reporting an active experimental multiplier.

The whole-parent search locates Linear.get_tensors as the direct inner-export caller. It supplies self.key only for a loaded layer. Conversion collects these dictionaries, saves them, and reloads from the same dictionary; Model.get_storage_info and the evaluation adapter consume values for byte accounting. These consumers retain compatible dictionary usage, although a present zero multiplier now contributes storage bytes. The FP16 alternatives keep their existing get_tensors(key) interface; no LinearEXL3 subclass appeared in the class-name search.

A bounded Python check compared the extracted parent method with a transcription of the replacement using fake tensors. Absent and nonzero metadata produced matching key sets; present zero metadata added exactly k.mcg and k.mul1. This checks selection logic, not real tensor contiguity or saved-file compatibility.

annotation.summary: Consolidates EXL3 tensor export into a None-filtered comprehension, normalizing every exported tensor and retaining present zero-valued multiplier metadata.

argv:
import ast,pathlib,types
p=ast.parse(pathlib.Path('exllamav3/modules/quant/exl3.py').read_text()); c=next(n for n in p.body if isinstance(n,ast.ClassDef) and n.name=='LinearEXL3'); f=next(n for n in c.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name=='get_tensors'); ns={}; exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[f],type_ignores=[]),'parent','exec'),ns)
class T:
 def __init__(self,name): self.name=name; self.calls=0
 def contiguous(self): self.calls+=1; return self
names=['su','sv','suh','svh','trellis','bias','mcg','mul1']
def new(o): return {'k.'+s:t.contiguous() for s,t in [(s,getattr(o,s)) for s in names] if t is not None}
for v in [None,0,1]:
 o=types.SimpleNamespace(**{s:(T(s) if s in ['suh','svh','trellis'] or (s in ['mcg','mul1'] and v is not None) else None) for s in names},mcg_mult=v or 0,mul1_mult=v or 0)
 old=ns['get_tensors'](o,'k'); before={s:getattr(o,s).calls for s in ['mcg','mul1'] if getattr(o,s) is not None}; out=new(o)
 print(v,sorted(old),sorted(out),'old_metadata_contiguous_calls',before)
 assert set(old)<=set(out)
 assert set(out)-set(old)==({'k.mcg','k.mul1'} if v==0 else set())
print('selection checks passed; fake tensors only')
